arguments.value: Kiromic, Inc. hired Gianluca Rotino as an independent consultant starting July 1, 2018. He was to provide business, marketing, and strategy support, including analysis, business development, clinical pipeline priorities, and managing consulting duties, and be paid $400 per hour for up to 19 hours per month unless preapproved otherwise. The agreement requires him to keep the company’s confidential information private, avoid using others’ trade secrets, and return company materials when the relationship ends. Any work product or inventions created while performing the services belong to the company, and he must help the company secure related intellectual property rights. The agreement can be ended by either side with written notice, and the company must pay for completed work owed at termination. He is treated as an independent contractor, not an employee, must comply with debarment and conflict-of-interest rules, and may not subcontract or assign the agreement without consent. The contract includes standard tax, severability, entire-agreement, and Texas-law provisions, and disputes must be resolved by binding arbitration in Houston, Texas.
